goodtidings_trader_arrives: Dagny, a wandering trader, is riding up on Atlas
goodtidings_trader_closed: Dagny has packed up and is moving on
goodtidings_trader_greet1: Who is... never mind. What are you buying?
goodtidings_trader_greet2: Well met, Viking. I trade, I don't beg, and I don't give.
goodtidings_trader_greet3: Atlas and I go where the trade is good. It led us here.
goodtidings_trader_greet4: Odin sent you to this world to fight. I came to it to trade.
goodtidings_trader_greet5: Don't tell Haldor you saw me. His prices are a crime.
goodtidings_trader_hello1: I don't deal in charity. I deal in fair prices.
goodtidings_trader_hello2: Everything here was earned. Nothing here is free.
goodtidings_trader_hello3: Look all you like. Haggling is for Fulings.
goodtidings_trader_hello4: Coin for goods, goods for coin. No gods need be involved.
goodtidings_trader_hello5: Hildir sells hats. I sell what keeps you alive.
goodtidings_trader_bought1: Value for value. The only honest trade.
goodtidings_trader_bought2: You earned that. Spend it well.
goodtidings_trader_bought4: May it serve you better than the gods ever did.
goodtidings_trader_bought5: Spoken like someone who knows what a thing is worth.
goodtidings_trader_sold1: A fair exchange. The world runs on those.
goodtidings_trader_sold2: Good work fetches a good price. Remember that.
goodtidings_trader_sold3: Coin well earned. Even the Dvergr would agree.
goodtidings_trader_sold4: I'll find a buyer. I always do.
goodtidings_trader_goodbye1: Keep the motor of the world turning, friend.
goodtidings_trader_goodbye3: Build something worth trading for. I'll be back.
goodtidings_trader_goodbye4: Atlas waits for no one. Neither do I.
goodtidings_trader_leaving2: Dagny packs her wares, and Atlas lumbers off down the road.
goodtidings_trader_leaving3: Dagny has better markets to reach before nightfall.
goodtidings_trader_talk1: The motor of the world runs on those who make things.
goodtidings_trader_talk2: I never asked anyone to live for my sake. Not even Odin.
goodtidings_trader_talk3: Atlas carries the whole load. He has never once complained.
goodtidings_trader_talk4: My brother ran our family's trade route into a swamp. I run a Lox.
goodtidings_trader_talk5: Ymir's bones make good ground for a road, if anyone would build one.
goodtidings_trader_talk6: The Dvergr understand. You don't ask, you offer something in return.
goodtidings_trader_talk7: Haldor hides in a forest and waits. I go where the customers are.
goodtidings_trader_talk8: Every hall in this world was built by someone who wanted it built.
goodtidings_trader_talk9: Ten worlds on the great tree, and not one honest market among them.
goodtidings_trader_talk10: If the gods wanted it given away, they'd have left it lying in a chest.
goodtidings_atlas_munch3: Atlas eats it in one gulp.
goodtidings_atlas_fed1: Atlas munches happily. Dagny knocks 30% off:
goodtidings_atlas_fed2: Atlas crunches away, delighted. Dagny marks down:
goodtidings_atlas_fed3: A well-fed Lox makes a generous trader. 30% off:
goodtidings_bountiful1: A warm season settles over your home. Everything stirs and grows.
goodtidings_bountiful2: A breath of summer passes over your home. The land is generous today.
goodtidings_bountiful3: The air smells of honey and new leaves. Your home is bountiful.
goodtidings_muninn_arrives: A white raven lands near your home. Muninn has a question.
goodtidings_muninn_nothing: Muninn looks at you, and finds too little in your memory to ask about. Yet.
goodtidings_muninn_answered_wrong: $1 answered Muninn wrongly. The beasts heard his cry.
goodtidings_muninn_right1: You remember well. Odin will hear of it.
goodtidings_muninn_right2: Memory is worth more than gold. Take this, then.
goodtidings_muninn_right3: Rightly said. I fly back to the High One.
goodtidings_muninn_wrong1: Forgotten! Krahh! Let the carrion-eaters come!
goodtidings_muninn_wrong2: Wrong. The wolves and I have an understanding.
goodtidings_muninn_wrong3: A short memory makes a short life. Krahh!
goodtidings_riddle_craft:
I remember $1, shaped together $2.
What did they become?
goodtidings_riddle_drop:
One who falls leaves $1 behind.
Who is it?
goodtidings_riddle_station:
I remember $1 being made.
Where was it made?
goodtidings_riddle_boss:
What must be laid on the altar
to wake $1?
goodtidings_riddle_grows:
Only one land grows $1.
Which is it?
goodtidings_lore1_q:
Eight legs he runs on, the swiftest of steeds;
whose horse is he, and what is he called?
goodtidings_lore2_q:
From his flesh the earth was made, from his blood the sea,
from his skull the sky. Who was he?
goodtidings_lore3_q:
Its roots reach three wells, its boughs over all nine worlds.
Name the tree.
goodtidings_lore4_q:
Odin gave an eye for one drink from a well of wisdom.
Whose well?
goodtidings_lore5_q:
It never misses and always returns to the hand that threw it.
Whose hammer, and what is it called?
goodtidings_lore6_q:
Dwarves forged it, and it never misses its mark.
What is Odin's spear called?
goodtidings_lore7_q:
Burning in three colours, it bridges Midgard and Asgard.
What is it called?
goodtidings_lore8_q:
Bound with a ribbon made from a cat's footfall and a woman's beard,
he will swallow Odin at the end. Who?
goodtidings_lore9_q:
He lies in the sea, around all Midgard, biting his own tail.
Name him.
goodtidings_lore10_q:
Beneath the world tree he gnaws its roots and the corpses of oathbreakers.
Who is he?
goodtidings_lore11_q:
Odin eats nothing, and gives the meat on his table to two beasts.
What are they called?
goodtidings_lore12_q:
Five hundred and forty doors, a roof of shields, and the slain feast there.
Whose hall?
goodtidings_lore13_q:
He needs less sleep than a bird, and hears the grass grow.
Who guards the bridge?
goodtidings_lore14_q:
When the end comes, one horn will sound over all the worlds.
What is it called?
goodtidings_lore15_q:
Built from the nails of the dead, it will carry the giants to the last battle.
Name the ship.
goodtidings_lore16_q:
Two dwarves killed the wisest of men and mixed his blood with honey.
Who were they?
goodtidings_lore17_q:
He waits in Muspelheim, and at the end his blade of fire will burn the worlds.
Who is he?
goodtidings_lore18_q:
Four rivers of milk ran from her udders, and she fed the first giant.
Who was she?
goodtidings_lore19_q:
She stands on Valhalla's roof, and mead flows from her udders for the slain.
What is she?
goodtidings_lore20_q:
Cooked every night and whole again every morning, he feeds the einherjar.
Who is he?
goodtidings_lore21_q:
He runs up and down the world tree, carrying insults between eagle and dragon.
Who?
goodtidings_lore22_q:
I fly out each morning with my brother and return each night to Odin's shoulder.
What does my name mean?
goodtidings_lore23_q:
He stands on Valhalla's roof and eats from the tree; from his antlers the rivers flow.
What is the stag called?
goodtidings_lore24_q: Into which world did Odin cast the Forsaken, those he defeated?
goodtidings_lore25_q: Who brought you to Valheim, to prove yourself against his enemies?
goodtidings_lore26_q:
In the last battle, a son of Odin will tear Fenrir's jaws apart with his shoe.
Which son?
goodtidings_dverger_arrives: A wounded Dvergr is staggering toward your home.
goodtidings_dverger_feed: Give him food from your hotbar
goodtidings_dverger_hungry: He looks at your hands, hopefully. Food, from your hotbar.
goodtidings_dverger_helped1: Hrm. A fire. Somewhere warm, friend, that's all I ask.
goodtidings_dverger_helped2: Help? From a surface-dweller? ...I'll take it.
goodtidings_dverger_helped3: Easy. Easy. Point me to your hearth.
goodtidings_dverger_nofire1: No fire? Then the cold ground will have to do.
goodtidings_dverger_nofire2: Not even a hearth. I'll sit here, then.
goodtidings_dverger_rest1: Ahh. Better. Is there anything to eat?
goodtidings_dverger_rest2: I could eat a Lox. Or anything, really.
goodtidings_dverger_fed1: Mm. More, if you have it.
goodtidings_dverger_full1: Enough, enough. Let me rest a moment.
goodtidings_dverger_full2: My hands are steady again. Give me a moment.
goodtidings_dverger_thanks1: You've a Dvergr's thanks. And a Dvergr's craft. Come here.
goodtidings_dverger_thanks2: Hold still. Let me see to that gear.
goodtidings_dverger_thanks3: That gear of yours has seen better days. Let me look.
goodtidings_dverger_neglected1: Left to rot by surface folk. My kin will hear of this.
goodtidings_dverger_neglected2: So this is your hospitality. Remember it.
goodtidings_dverger_neglected3: I go. But the Dvergr remember.
goodtidings_dverger_left: The wounded Dvergr limps away, cursing your name.
goodtidings_dverger_band: The Dvergr have come for those who left their kin to suffer.
goodtidings_tempered_tip: Mended by a Dvergr's hands: your gear wears down slower.
goodtidings_tempered_start: The Dvergr mended and tempered your gear.
goodtidings_dverger_needfire: He's shivering, too cold to eat. Light a fire near him.
goodtidings_dverger_cold1: Too cold... too cold to eat. A fire, friend. Please.
goodtidings_dverger_cold2: No warmth here. I can't keep anything down like this.
goodtidings_dverger_firefound1: A fire! Bless you. Help me over there.
goodtidings_dverger_firefound2: Warmth, at last. I'm coming, I'm coming.
goodtidings_dverger_done1: Mended and tempered. It'll serve you a while yet.
goodtidings_dverger_done2: There. Better than new. Farewell, friend.
goodtidings_skald_arrives: A long-dead skald rises at your hearth. Gather round and listen.
goodtidings_skald_leaves: The skald's song ends. He sinks back to his rest.
goodtidings_skald_inspired: The old song stirs your memory: your skills rise.
goodtidings_skald_risen1: Ahh. A hearth, and folk around it. Good.
goodtidings_skald_risen2: Who wakes old bones? No matter. I have songs.
goodtidings_skald_risen3: Mind me, just stretching. It's been a few hundred winters.
goodtidings_skald_begin1: Gather round! Hear now the songs of the north.
goodtidings_skald_begin2: Sit, friends. Let the old songs do their work.
goodtidings_skald_begin3: This one's older than your grandsire's grandsire.
goodtidings_skald_between2: My father taught me this one. Before the worms did.
goodtidings_skald_between3: Ha! You liked that. One more.
goodtidings_skald_bow3: Remember the songs. That's all a skald asks.
